contradiction_resolution: No contradiction with any cross-checked claim (CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, RED-0001) or corroborated finding. FND-0005 (corroborated) already acknowledges the residual caveat about ordered distinct reduced support in its adjudication reason ('Mild residual caveat (ordered distinct reduced support of the unique/general member of |L|) does not restore emptiness of Z as a locus'). FND-0083 formalizes this caveat as a standalone scope-limitation finding. FND-0063 (corroborated) gives the failure condition O_C(Γ)≅L without asserting reduced-support nonemptiness. FND-0064 (corroborated) identifies Conf_6→reduced-support open as a finite etale S_6-torsor, which presupposes the base is nonempty. FND-0073 (corroborated) shows h^0(L)=1+h^0(M) with deg(M)=4; when h^0(M)=0, h^0(L)=1 and |L|≅P^0 is a single point which may be a non-reduced divisor. The finding correctly identifies that χ(L)=1 alone (giving h^0(L)≥1) proves only Sym^6-fibre nonemptiness, not reduced-support nonemptiness on every geometric fibre. Mathematical verification: for a degree-6 line bundle on a genus-6 curve with χ=1, the unique effective divisor (when h^0=1) can be non-reduced (e.g., concentrated at fewer than 6 points); the reduced-support open is Zariski-open in |L| but may be empty when |L| is a single non-reduced point. This is a genuine logical gap in any argument that relies solely on RR to establish Z_ev nonemptiness.

scope.locus: reduced-support open in |L| and ordered Conf_6 incidence Z_ev
